findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on properly washing their hands. Ensure that all staff are trained to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands to prevent recontaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The dish shelf and the table next to the preparation area holding pizza pans. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The NUDO board to the left of the preparation table is cracked.
2. The trim in the left corner above the triple sink is cracked. 
3. A ceiling tile above the pizza boxes next to the pizza oven is observed to be in a state of disrepair. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are repaired and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following physical facilities were observed to be in need of a cleaning: 

1. The ceiling vent above the front register. 
2. The ceiling tiles next to the office have an accumulation of dust on them. 
3. The wall above the cook line has an accumulation of food debris. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and then maintained cleaned as often as necessary. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: 2-102.12: Observed no CFM on duty during inspection when food was being prepared. The manager’s CFPM license expired in February 2023. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of food preparation and operation. CFPM class information was given to the manager.  (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment:

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: Observed rollers in pizza oven to be soiled with food debris and residue. Clean and sanitize rollers. (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-501.110: Observed coat stored on top of large dough mixer. Store employee coats in a designated area. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: 2-102.12: Observed manager on duty to have an expired certified food manager certification.  (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11  (Pf) Spatula is observed peeling and chipped. Utensil is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.  Discarded during inspection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed opened personal bottles being stored on middle shelving within the 2-door sliding cooler. Discarded during inspection. Store personal foods separated and on the lowest (suggested using a tub to contain and separate). Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-153(a) Observed a container of pizza sauce just pulled from the cooler without a time indicated on the container. Time indicated on the container for Time as Control during the inspection. When using time as a control. Food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-260 Observed the only available make cooler to not be cold holding properly. The unit is being turned off and on each day in order to prevent overnight freezing. Facility is going to be using time as control on foods throughout the evening. The facility need not worry about olives and fresh produce. Meats, cheese, and tomatoes should be moved through within four hours or discarded. Portions being stocked are smaller than normal. Will spot check tomorrow. Cooler may need more time to reach proper cold holding temperature - only an hour was given today. Enough hot or cold storage units used for displaying potentially hazardous foods shall be provided to maintain proper product temperature requirements.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) The thermometer present in the make cooler appears to be off about ten degrees. The facility is using this thermometer to determine when food may be returned to the cooler so it needs to be accurate. Two stem thermometers from SCDPH indicated a temperature of 48 in the base and 51 in the top. See violation #4.  All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Overall, facility is observed clean and in good repair. The floor-to-wall joint behind tables, cooler, and shelving is observed minimally soiled with accumulated grease and flour. Clean the floors paying attention to this area around the kitchen. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: REPEAT 1x> 1) Observed the gasket of the Victory hot holding cabinet to be in a state of disrepair and held together by tape. Replace gasket that is free from gaps or cracks and is in sound condition to allow for easy cleaning. NEW 2) Observed the front cover of the prep cooler where the refrigeration coils are located to be missing its cover. Provide a properly constructed prep cooler to allow for easily cleaning. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

Observed wet and soiled wiping cloths stored on the counter top. Store wiping cloths in sanitizing solution between uses or dispose of in soiled linens storage.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to be soiled with rust. Replace blade or remove rust to provide for a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1x> Facility is unable to provide a certified IL-Food Service Sanitation Manager. Staff noted he had recently taken his exam and passed although has not submitted the application to IDPH to obtain his certificate. A FSSMC request form was provided. Once staff receives his FSSMC card, email or fax over card information to inspector to correct the violation and avoid a follow up inspection.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize this food contact surface before use or at least once every four hours if it will be used on a continual basis.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Scoop in sugar bin had fallen down into sugar.  CORRECTED - scoop was righted so handle extended up out of sugar.  As amount of sugar gets low, and cannot support scoop, consider storing scoop on a clean and dry surface (see Food Code reference below).
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Upon start of inspection, there were no paper towels available at hand sink.  CORRECTED - paper towels were provided at sink.  Make sure all staff understand importance of supplying paper towels and soap as soon as they run out.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
